cards.explanation: The answer is True. Paul says what you sow “…is not the body that will be, but just a seed, perhaps of wheat or something else.” (1 Corinthians 15:37). Nobody plants a seed and expects to see that same little seed standing there in July. The seed is just where it starts.

The answer is God. Paul says “…God gives it a body as He has designed, and to each kind of seed He gives its own body.” (1 Corinthians 15:38). The farmer drops the seed and walks off, friends. The body is God's doing.

The answer is that each has its own kind. Paul says “Men have one kind of flesh, animals have another, birds another, and fish another.” (1 Corinthians 15:39). One list, four kinds. Nobody gets mixed up in this lineup.

The answer is False. Paul says “The sun has one degree of splendor, the moon another, and the stars another; and star differs from star in splendor.” (1 Corinthians 15:41). The sun, the moon and the stars each get their own degree. Even star differs from star, and I know a few skies where that's easy to see.

The answer is imperishable. Paul says “What is sown is perishable; it is raised imperishable.” (1 Corinthians 15:42). Perishable means it can wear out, friends. Imperishable means it won't. My edges could use that kind of news.

The answer is glory. Paul says “It is sown in dishonor; it is raised in glory.” (1 Corinthians 15:43). It's the same body, and the ending is nothing like the start. What is sown in dishonor is raised in glory, and he follows it with weakness turning into power.

The answer is a spiritual body. Paul says “It is sown a natural body; it is raised a spiritual body.” (1 Corinthians 15:44). Then he adds, “If there is a natural body, there is also a spiritual body.” He treats the second as just as real as the first.

The answer is a life-giving spirit. Paul says “The first man Adam became a living being”; the last Adam “…a life-giving spirit.” (1 Corinthians 15:45). The first one became a living being, friends. The last one gives life.

The answer is True. Paul says “The spiritual, however, was not first, but the natural, and then the spiritual.” (1 Corinthians 15:46). That's the order. Natural first, spiritual after, like mixing the dough before the oven.

The answer is heaven. Paul says “The first man was of the dust of the earth, the second man from heaven.” (1 Corinthians 15:47). Dust for one, heaven for the other. Two very different starting points.

The answer is False. Paul says “…flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God, nor does the perishable inherit the imperishable.” (1 Corinthians 15:50). The perishable can't inherit the imperishable, friends. That's why the change in the next verses matters.

The answer is changed. Paul says “We will not all sleep, but we will all be changed…” (1 Corinthians 15:51). Some sleep and some don't, but nobody is left out of the change. All of us means all of us.

The answer is in the twinkling of an eye. Paul says it happens “…in an instant, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet.” (1 Corinthians 15:52). He adds that the dead will be raised imperishable, and we will be changed. That's how quick the change is.

The answer is immortality. Paul says “…the perishable must be clothed with the imperishable, and the mortal with immortality.” (1 Corinthians 15:53). Paul talks about being clothed, friends, like putting on something new. Mortal gets covered by immortality.

The answer is that death is swallowed up in victory. The saying is “Death has been swallowed up in victory.” (1 Corinthians 15:54). Death is the one getting swallowed, friends. Not the other way around.
The answer is sin. Paul says “The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law.” (1 Corinthians 15:56). He names sin as the sting of death. Then he adds that the power of sin is the law.

The answer is that their labor in the Lord is not in vain. Paul says “Always excel in the work of the Lord, because you know that your labor in the Lord is not in vain.” (1 Corinthians 15:58). Not in vain means it counts, friends. So keep those ovens warm.
